subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw add linux/riscv64 as an official Docker release platform now, and should that platform remain non-blocking for existing amd64/arm64 releases?
rationale: This expands official release infrastructure and support expectations rather than fixing an already-defined broken release contract, so maintainers need to own the platform policy and validation bar.

options.title: Add non-blocking riscv64 images
options.body: Build riscv64 through QEMU, publish its digest only when successful, and require live release-path proof before treating it as official.

options.title: Defer official riscv64 images
options.body: Keep the request open until dependency, Codex runtime, and release-capacity concerns are resolved.

options.title: Use an experimental image path first
options.body: Publish riscv64 outside the main multi-arch manifest until reliability and support expectations are clear.

recommendation.title: Add non-blocking riscv64 images
recommendation.body: Build riscv64 through QEMU, publish its digest only when successful, and require live release-path proof before treating it as official.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker Hub, release-control, Dockerfile, and docs history makes this the best available owner for the Docker release platform decision.
